comparison: Perfect alignment on occupancy modeling results (C33-C39, C128-C130). Both find the analyses adequate and results supported. Peer review suggests adding anthropogenic disturbance considerations but does not challenge the presented findings.

Both address methodological claims about data collection (C26-C32, C123-C127). OpenEval finds methods well-documented, but peer reviewers identify significant concerns about unclear or inconsistent sampling effort reporting (280 vs 319/322 camera sites).

Strong agreement on temporal overlap analysis (C45-C52). Both affirm the kernel density methods and statistical testing are appropriate. Peer review explicitly states 'Temporal and dietary results are solid.'

Strong agreement on dietary analysis results (C53-C65, C75, C83, C94-C95). Both affirm DNA metabarcoding findings are solid. Peer review particularly highlights the importance of pika predation pressure findings for conservation.
Complete agreement on methodological strengths (C107-C108). Both explicitly praise the integration of camera trapping and DNA metabarcoding as providing robust, convincing evidence.

Strong agreement on conservation implications (C114-C117). Both affirm the importance of pika conservation and risks of poisoning campaigns. Peer review explicitly endorses these management implications.

Strong agreement on core conclusions about spatial partitioning as key coexistence mechanism (C23, C71, C111). Both find this main finding convincingly supported by the data, though OpenEval notes some causal claims are inferential.
Agreement on spatial overlap findings (C40-C43, C66). Both accept the low spatial overlap measurements as supported. Peer review affirms these quantitative results without challenge.
Agreement on summary claims about overlap patterns (C17-C22). Both find these synthesis claims well-supported by the detailed analyses, with peer review affirming conclusions are supported by data.

Agreement on broad synthesis about niche partitioning (C70). Both support this conclusion, though OpenEval notes it somewhat oversimplifies complex patterns. Peer review affirms the coexistence evidence is convincing.
Agreement on mesocarnivore coexistence mechanisms (C24, C87). Both find these interpretations logical and supported by the overlap data. Peer review accepts these as well-supported conclusions.

Agreement on apex-mesocarnivore interactions, particularly wolf-red fox case (C25, C102, C104-C105). Both find these interpretations supported by the data showing high temporal overlap with spatial/dietary differences.
Agreement on dietary composition and spatial partitioning connections (C75-C78, C86). Both find the link between prey preferences and habitat associations reasonable, though somewhat inferential.

Partial overlap on dietary findings (C94-C95). OpenEval notes the Pallas's cat competitive interaction inference (C110) is speculative due to insufficient spatial/temporal data. Peer review focuses on broader dietary results without specifically addressing this limitation.
OpenEval evaluates background/literature claims (C2-C16) as well-supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these contextual claims.
OpenEval evaluates additional contextual claims (C73-C74, C80-C82, C100) as appropriately cited. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these supporting literature claims.
OpenEval evaluates study site description (C118-C122) as factually supported. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these geographic/climatic descriptors.
